newsitem.title: USA: Golf-Couples sinks big putt to win Presidents Cup for U.S.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Couples sinks big putt to win Presidents Cup for U.S.

text.p: Fred Couples trickled in a 30-foot birdie putt to clinch a dramatic one-point victory for the United States over the International team in the Presidents Cup match play competition on Sunday.
The United States won 16 1/2 to 15 1/2, but only after a titanic struggle in the 12 final-day singles matches at the Robert Trent Jones Golf Club in Lake Manassas.
Couples, in the final singles match, needed to beat Vijay Singh of Fiji to win the Cup, and he did so at the 17th hole.
After the former Masters champion sank his birdie putt, Singh had to hole his 15-footer to keep the competition alive, but, bothered by a spike mark, he missed and it was all over.
"It was some match," said Couples. "What a thrill!"

It was a shattering end for the Internationals, comprising the best players from the rest of the world, except Europe. But they certainly made the Americans sweat, unlike the first event two years ago, which the U.S. team won by eight points.
"It would have been wonderful if we'd won, because I think we played well enough to do it," said International captain Peter Thomson.
"What a contest. I can't remember in my lifetime career anything as exciting and as emotional as that. The last hour has been almost heart-stopping. I'm very proud of my team."

Winning captain Arnold Palmer said: "I thought maybe it would be a little easier than it was. To have it end the way it did, I couldn't be happier. This is the longest week I have had in a long time."

The Internationals always had their work cut out after falling five points behind on the first day. They recovered to reduce the deficit to one point going into Sunday, but still needed to win seven of 12 singles matches to claim the Cup.
The United States turned the pressure on by winning five of the first seven singles contests and the International team had to sweep the last five.
But they stayed in the hunt as Australians Greg Norman and Steve Elkington, South Africa's Ernie Els and Frank Nobilo of New Zealand all won their matches.

Elkington holed a 25-footer at the last to beat Justin Leonard 1 up, Els defeated Phil Mickelson 3 and 2 in a battle of two of the world's best two young players, and Norman won four of his final five holes to beat Corey Pavin 3 and 1.
Nobilo, in the penultimate match, won his last five holes to down British Open champion Tom Lehman 3 and 2, leaving it to Couples and Singh to decide the cup.
Couples was 1 up with two holes left after Singh won the 16th, but his magnificent birdie at the next hole drove a dagger into the heart of the Internationals.
"We came to win, we did, and we beat a great 12 guys," Couples said. "I was a little edgy last night when I found out I was playing the last match and going against Vijay."
The best individual records belonged to Americans Mark O'Meara and David Duval. O'Meara won all five of his matches, while Duval won all four of his.
Best International was Els with three wins, one tie and one loss.
The next Presidents Cup is scheduled for 1998. It has not been decided yet whether it will be held in the United States again or go overseas.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
